title: Interest Days on Medicaid Plan Appeals — Insurance Coverage & Claims Appeals Timetable
content:
**Appeals timetable — Insurance Coverage & Claims, Medicaid Managed Care Plan plan appeals.** The plan appeal's interest days run according to how long the plan took between the date the claim reached it and its denial date (the latest denial date on the claim), measured in calendar days against the expected adjudication period of the coverage's payer class:

- where the plan took **more than twice** its expected adjudication days, interest runs for every calendar day from the date the claim reached it to today;
- where it took **more than** its expected adjudication days **but not more than twice** that, interest runs for the calendar days from that date to today less the expected adjudication days;
- **otherwise** no interest runs.

## Expected adjudication periods

| Payer class | Expected adjudication period (calendar days of filing) | More than this | More than twice this |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | 14 | 15 or more days | 29 or more days |
| Medicare Advantage Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Medicare Supplement Plan | 14 | 15 or more days | 29 or more days |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| TRICARE Prime and Select | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Commercial In-Network Plan | 30 | 31 or more days | 61 or more days |
| Commercial Out-of-Network Plan | 45 | 46 or more days | 91 or more days |

For a Medicaid Managed Care Plan coverage the period is 30 days.

## Worked days (hypothetical, expected period 30 days, claim reached the plan 140 days ago)

| Days to denial | Interest days |
|---|---|
| 61 | 140 |
| 60 | 140 less 30, 110 |
| 31 | 110 |
| 30 | 0 |
